title: System Overlay
concept: Five steps that turn a hard conversation into an actual outcome: warm up, make sure it's safe, say what happened, ask for one thing, agree on next steps.
whenToUse: Any sensitive conversation, request for change, repair, or decision you're making together. Use it as a checklist when you're stuck, going in circles, or things have escalated.
steps: Warm up — say the warmest true thing you can. Remind each other you're on the same team.
Make it safe — the relationship isn't at risk in this moment.
Say what happened — what happened, how it felt, what it meant.
Ask for one thing — specific, doable, with a timeframe.
Agree on next steps — who does what, by when, and when you'll check back in.

phrases.text: I love us, and I’m not trying to fight.
When X happened, I felt Y; the impact was Z.
Can we try ___ this week and check in on ___?

working: Warmed up → made it safe → “When you scrolled while I talked, I felt dismissed; I shut down.” Asked for 10 minutes device-free at night. Agreed to try it this week and check in Sunday.
notWorking: Jumping straight to a rule: “No phones at night — it's rude.” Without warming up, making it safe, and owning your side first, it lands as control, and the fight turns into “always/never.”
activity: A 12-minute practice run: pick something low-stakes, use all five steps out loud, listener keeps you on track. Aim for a little better, not perfect.
